transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Dana Liu (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Redwood CSM), Rajesh Kapoor (Lumina ML Eng), Emily Chen (Lumina SRE), Oliver Grant (Lumina Data Sci), Priya Nair (Lumina Infra)
Shared artifacts: benchmark sheet (link: drive.redwood/reports/lumina-quant-2026-10-13), sample prompts (drive.redwood/data/lumina-prompts-v2), infra runbook (internal)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45. Quick roll call, and then Dana will walk through the INT8/FP8 results you ran last week.
[00:10] Rajesh: Hey, Rajesh here. Emily, Oliver, Priya are on as well.
[00:15] Dana: Cool. So I pulled the sheet, I looked at Lumina's runs on the 7b and 13b variants. The headline: INT8 gives roughly 1.9-2.4x token throughput on our test harness, FP8 is about 1.5-1.8x depending on kernel. But quality, there's a bit of nuance.
[00:35] Oliver: Right, on the 13b we saw a soft drop in exact-match and a higher drop on the open-ended hallucination prompts. The top-5 prompt set we care about lost about 2-3% BLEU-ish style score for INT8, FP8 was closer to 1%.
[01:00] Dana: Yup, that matches what we saw. Also note the per-sequence latency tail - INT8 batching improves throughput but increases p95 slightly if KV cache miss patterns occur.
[01:20] Priya: Can you spell KV cache? In the notes it says "kee-vee cache" sometimes got transcribed odd.
[01:25] Marta: (laughs) Fireflies transcription did that earlier, yes.
[01:30] Emily: Quick infra note - our SRE runs were on a shared spot cluster; we think noisy neighbor might have pushed some of the tail numbers. We'll confirm once we switch to the dedicated test cluster.
[01:45] Samir: Good call. Samir here - also to add, when we ran INT8 on similar workloads we saw bit-flip at certain activation ranges unless we did activation range clipping + per-channel scales. Dana's recommended config includes that.
[02:05] Dana: Exactly. Suggested next test: asymmetric per-channel quant with 8-bit activations, plus 16-bit accumulators (simulated on A100). Also run calibration using 1k representative prompts, not just random tokens.
[02:30] Rajesh: For calibration we used the standard wiki+in-domain mix of 800/200, but maybe skewing to more in-domain will help.
[02:40] Dana: Yes, skew to in-domain. Also try layer-wise higher precision for first and last transformer blocks - freezing them to FP16 while quantizing the middle layers to INT8 often recovers most of the quality.
[02:58] Oliver: That matches our internal hypothesis. We can test freezing 2 layers at top and bottom.
[03:10] Samir: On the FP8 side, results looked pretty stable, but FP8 hardware path depends on kernel availability - some older kernels fall back to emulation and you lose perf. Which vendor kernels did you hit?
[03:30] Emily: We were on CUDA 12.4 with mixed vendor builds. On one run, FP8 took a fallback and we lost the perf benefit.
[03:40] Dana: That's expected. We'll note kernel versions in the sheet. We can recommend a set of tested combinations (CUDA, cuDNN, driver).
[03:50] Rajesh: Any guidance on expected cost delta? If INT8 doubles throughput but introduces 2-3% quality loss, how do we think about the cost-quality tradeoff operationally?
[04:05] Samir: We put a cost model in the shared sheet - rough back-of-envelope: INT8 reduces token-cost by ~45-55% for generation workload due to doubling throughput on same hardware, but if you need to bump to a larger model to regain quality that erodes savings. That's why per-prompt eval matters.
[04:30] Oliver: We ran a small rerank workflow - the reranker is more sensitive; INT8 caused noticeable lower re-rank accuracy. Might need hybrid approach: use INT8 for candidate generation and FP16/FP8 for rerank.
[04:50] Dana: Hybrid is a common pattern. Also consider caching full KV for common prefixes so rerank doesn't recompute.
[05:05] Priya: On the access side, we'll provision a dedicated test cluster: 2xA100-equivalent and we'll lock network to Redwood SAs. ETA 2026-10-18, pending procurement.
[05:20] Emily: We'll also send SSH bastion details to Samir and Dana.
[05:30] Samir: Great. Back to tuning: Dana, can you summarize concrete configs we want them to run this week?
[05:40] Dana: Sure - 1) INT8 asymmetric per-channel with activation clipping (calibrate with in-domain 1k prompts), 2) Hybrid FP16 for first/last 2 blocks + INT8 middle, 3) FP8 fast-path where kernel available, note fallback, 4) Batch sizes sweep for latency/throughput tradeoffs (batch 1/2/4/8), 5) Evaluate rerank candidate suite separately. We'll log p50/p95/p99 and quality metrics (exact-match, EM-like, and a custom utility score).
[06:20] Rajesh: For quality metrics, Oliver will provide the utility scoring function - it's a weighted combo of correctness and hallucination penalty.
[06:35] Oliver: I'll drop the eval scripts and weighting in the shared drive by EOD 2026-10-16.
[06:45] Samir: Cool. A couple of notes on measurement: ensure you use same random seeds for sampling, and record temperature/topk/top-p settings. Small changes to sampling can look like model regressions.
[07:00] Emily: Noted. One more infra question: will Redwood need elevated access to our VPC logs or just model artifacts?
[07:10] Marta: From our side we'll only need read-only access to the test instances plus ability to push small benchmarking containers. No access to prod logs. We'll provide a runbook.
[07:25] Priya: Ok we'll whitelist the Redwood service account to the test subnet.
[07:30] Dana: Regarding failure modes: we observed on INT8 a tokenization edge-case where numeric tables get quantized poorly, causing repeated token outputs. We'll add a small prompt-correction test to the eval set.
[07:50] Rajesh: I saw that in two of our medical table prompts - it's important to flag since downstream extractors break.
[08:00] Samir: Good catch. Action: Oliver add 25 table-style prompts.
[08:10] Oliver: Will do.
[08:15] Samir: Any other vendor questions? Rajesh earlier mentioned Vertex and Cerebras comparisons - do you want us to include those bench numbers?
[08:30] Rajesh: If you have rough numbers it helps us decision-wise.
[08:35] Samir: We'll add a row comparing our hosted numbers vs public Vertex docs and internal Cerebras runs, with caveats. Expect that in the sheet Samir sends.
[08:50] Emily: One procedural note - procurement asked for an SOW outline if we move to dedicated. Is that something we can get after the next benchmark?
[09:00] Marta: Yes, we can draft a short SOW describing dedicated pool sizing, support SLAs, and data handling. We'll aim to share a draft by 2026-10-22.
[09:10] Priya: On encryption/KMS: we need to ensure keys remain in our KMS, any model artifacts stored must be encrypted-at-rest with our KMS. Is that supported in Private, but for dedicated how does key management look?
[09:25] Dana: Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS integration depending on provider. We'll include options in the SOW draft.
[09:40] Oliver: Also curious about audit logs and model version pinning - if we roll back quantized config, can we record which model+quant config produced which outputs?
[09:55] Samir: Yes, Redwood's console provides model versioning and per-request metadata (quant profile, kernel version, seed) saved to audit logs if enabled. We'll show you a sample export in the next call.
[10:15] Rajesh: Good. Any known blockers on our side?
[10:20] Priya: Procurement timeline may be 2-3 weeks; infra will ready cluster by 10-18 as said.
[10:30] Samir: Ok to recap next steps: Samir share benchmark sheet and cost/latency doc; Dana to run per-layer tests and configs; Lumina to provision test cluster and share access; Oliver to upload eval prompts and weighting; Marta to draft SOW; all to reconvene for deep-dive week of 2026-10-19.
[10:55] Rajesh: Sounds good. One last small ask: can you note the exact CUDA/cuDNN versions that pass our FP8 fast-path so we can align infra?
[11:05] Dana: We'll put that in the sheet - early recommendation: CUDA 12.6 + cuDNN 9.x and driver >= 535, but we'll verify exact patch levels.
[11:20] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll close the recording.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription errors: "kee-vee cache" instead of KV cache in a few spots, minor speaker attribution errors at ~00:15 that were corrected in notes.
notes: Shared drive links: drive.redwood/reports/lumina-quant-2026-10-13 (benchmarks), drive.redwood/data/lumina-prompts-v2 (prompts). SOW draft to come. Medium transcription quality - occasional mis-hears.
